title: Engineering
description: Review code boundaries, dependencies and compatibility before choosing an implementation.
questions: Which existing modules and interfaces can handle the change?
What happens to existing data and clients during rollout?
Which contracts or architecture decisions should the change document?

specialists.title: Software architect
specialists.focus: Trace the use case through the existing modules. Choose where the behavior and its dependencies belong and name the owner of any new boundary.

specialists.title: API and integration engineer
specialists.focus: Check changed request, response and event contracts against every supported consumer. Decide which changes need a compatibility path or migration.

specialists.title: Data engineer
specialists.focus: Identify the invariants for reads and writes. Check what happens to committed data when work is interrupted, retried or performed concurrently.

specialists.title: Code reviewer
specialists.focus: Find unnecessary dependencies and duplicated domain logic. Confirm that the proposed change can be verified through the entry points callers use.

evidence: Entry point, owning modules, changed behavior and the relevant repository paths or design decision.
Before-and-after public contracts and a list of supported callers or event consumers, with compatibility results for affected versions.
Data schema and migration sequence, with results for existing records, mixed-version rollout and the agreed recovery path where relevant.
Tests or execution traces that show success, a representative partial failure and a retry for operations that can repeat.
Reason for any new service or dependency and the name of the team expected to maintain it.
challenge: Could an existing module own this behavior without introducing a second source of truth?
Which supported caller or previously stored value would behave differently with the proposed change?
What has already been committed if the second step fails, and what happens when the request is retried?
Which edge of the new design requires another team to change or deploy at the same time?
decision_criteria: Prefer the design with a clear owner, the smallest affected boundary and a demonstrated test path for the agreed behavior.
Ask for a migration or consumer approval if a supported API, event or stored shape would break.
Hold the change when a foreseeable failure, retry or concurrent operation can break a data invariant without a verified recovery path.
Record the reason and responsible team when the change adds an operational dependency.
